<b>Вегетативная (автономная) нервная сис: The autonomic nervous system runs the organs without our conscious control. The sympathetic division (orange) leaves the thoracic and lumbar segments T1–L2 through the sympathetic trunk — a chain of ganglia along the spine. The parasympathetic (green) leaves the brainstem (nerves III, VII, IX and the vagus X) and the sacral segments S2–S4.
<b>«Бей или беги»</b> — симпатика. Зрачк: “Fight or flight” — sympathetic. Pupils dilate, the heart beats faster and harder, bronchi widen, the liver releases glucose and the adrenals pour adrenaline into the blood. Digestion stalls and the bladder relaxes: anything that does not help survival right now is put off.
<b>«Отдыхай и переваривай»</b> — парасим: “Rest and digest” — parasympathetic, mostly the vagus nerve. The pulse slows, pupils narrow, bronchi narrow a little, saliva and digestive juices flow, the gut churns food and the bladder contracts. Both divisions work all the time; only the balance shifts.
<b>Два нейрона и медиаторы.</b> Путь из: Two neurons and transmitters. The path from the brain to an organ is a chain of two neurons with a ganglion in between. In the ganglia of both divisions the transmitter is acetylcholine (nicotinic receptors). At the organ the sympathetic releases norepinephrine, the parasympathetic acetylcholine again (muscarinic receptors). The adrenal medulla is a modified ganglion: it releases adrenaline straight into the blood.
Сердце, зрачки, кишка и железы работают: Heart, pupils, gut and glands work without our knowing. Two divisions — an “accelerator” and a “brake” — keep pulling the body toward flight or toward rest.
\n <div><h2>Два отдела</h2>\n:
Two divisions

Sympathetic: centers in the lateral horns of spinal segments T1–L2; short preganglionic fibers → ganglia of the sympathetic trunk and prevertebral ganglia (celiac, mesenteric) → long postganglionic fibers to the organs. Parasympathetic: brainstem nuclei (with nerves III, VII, IX, X) and sacral segments S2–S4; long preganglionic fibers → ganglia next to or inside the organ → short postganglionic fibers. The vagus nerve carries about 75 % of parasympathetic fibers.

A third division is the enteric nervous system in the gut wall (≈ 500 million neurons): it runs peristalsis on its own, and the autonomic divisions only tune it.

Transmitters and drugs

  • Acetylcholine in the ganglia (nicotinic receptors) and at parasympathetic targets (muscarinic): atropine blocks them — the pupil dilates and the pulse speeds up.
  • Norepinephrine at sympathetic targets: β-blockers slow the heart, β₂-agonists (salbutamol) open the bronchi in asthma.
  • Exception: sweat glands receive sympathetic fibers that use acetylcholine.

Conventions

  • The main pathways of one side of the body are shown; in reality the nerves are paired and branch into plexuses.
  • Organs are simplified shapes in schematic positions; trunk ganglia are drawn evenly spaced.
  • Organ responses are sped up and exaggerated; both divisions are always active, the scheme shows the shift in balance.
